transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-07-10
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Sec), Ethan Cole (Nova CISO), Maya Liu (Nova Sec Eng), Oliver Grant (Nova DevOps)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of the external penetration test results run by third-party Redwest Security (note: vendor transcript mis-heard as Redwest), discussion of remediations, patch cadence, secure SDLC integration, and evidence needed for Nova's SOC 2/ISO audit. Agreement to run a retest after the initial patch wave.

Topics: pen-test findings, CVE triage, patching cadence, SCA/CI gating, RBAC/SSO gaps, audit log retention, KMS/CMK questions, SOC2 evidence package.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — we should have, uh, the Nova team and our security folks on the line. Marcus, you want to open with the high level?
[00:17] Marcus: yeah, thanks Lena. Hi Ethan, Maya, Oliver. So we ran the external pentest in late June — third party vendor, scope was public endpoints and our control plane APIs. Main call out: three critical class findings initially, about a dozen high, a handful of medium. We did prioritize by exploitability. There was one false positive flagged in the web auth flow, we think it's an auth header parsing difference, so that went to medium once validated.
[01:02] Ethan: uh can you list the three criticals again? I got the summary but want the exacts.
[01:07] Marcus: sure. Criticals: 1) outdated JWT library vulnerable to algorithm confusion (CVE-2024-12345) — that allows an attacker to craft tokens if they can get a signing key, 2) worker-image contained an old OpenSSL build with CVE-2024-21098 that allows remote decryption in some edge cases, 3) a misconfigured s3 policy on backups exposing metadata (not the blob data) to the public if someone guessed the URL — low probability but high impact for metadata leakage.
[01:48] Maya: so the S3 one, is that the backup meta bucket? We thought we had blocking rules.
[01:53] Marcus: yes, it's the meta bucket; the object ACLs were inherited from an older template — team had recently changed infra-as-code and that template slipped in. We recommend applying the deny-public-policy and explicit bucket ACLs, and rotate any keys that touched the affected backup process.
[02:20] Oliver: do you have the exact buckets listed in the report? I couldn't find them in the quick summary.
[02:25] Marcus: yep, in the raw logs we included s3://nova-backups/meta-2024 and a note — we'll share the full artifact.
[02:31] Lena: action item — we'll upload the full PDF and raw trace logs to the shared link after this call.
[02:38] Ethan: good — we need that for the ISO audit pack too.
[02:44] Priya: quick note on the JWT issue: for customers using our hosted API, we have a migration plan — patch then rotate signing keys with zero-downtime rollout. For dedicated/private customers it's slightly different but same approach.
[03:00] Maya: question on KMS — the report mentions CMKs and key rotation, does Redwood support external KMS (BYOK)?
[03:07] Marcus: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; you can bring your own CMK from AWS KMS or an HSM-backed key. We did mention in the report the current dev cluster used Redwood-managed keys and that was flagged as needing rotation.
[03:26] Oliver: can you confirm the envelope encryption flow? Our legal wants the proof that blob data is unreadable without the CMK.
[03:32] Priya: we'll provide the encryption-at-rest diagram and a sample decryption flow showing that without the CMK the symmetric DEKs are useless. We'll include HSM mention and KMS key rotation policy.
[03:50] Ethan: audit logs — how long are logs kept and do you provide immutable export?
[03:55] Marcus: currently audit logs retention is 365 days by default for hosted; we can configure longer retention for enterprise customers. We also support export to customer S3 or syslog for long-term archival. Immutability via WORM buckets isn't baked in but can be deployed via bucket policies.
[04:18] Maya: for SOC 2, our auditor asked for proof of log integrity and chain of custody — can you provide hashes or signed bundles?
[04:26] Priya: yes, we can provide signed log bundles and chain of custody notes; we'll include a walk-through on how we generate the log digests.
[04:35] Lena: circling back to patch cadence — Nova, what's your current cadence? Weekly, monthly?
[04:40] Oliver: currently monthly for infra, weekly for critical hotfixes, but the process is manual because our pipeline gating is... we're still building out full SCA gating.
[04:52] Marcus: here is what we recommend: rapid emergency patch window for critical (24-72 hours), weekly for high, monthly for medium/low. And integrate SCA tools (Snyk/Dependabot) with CI so we block merges for critical CVEs.
[05:11] Maya: okay, that seems doable. Can Redwood provide CI gate scripts or example GitHub Actions?
[05:17] Marcus: yes, we'll drop a sample pipeline snippet and image-scanning config.
[05:22] Ethan: about secure SDLC — can you map where the findings originated? Was it code, dependency, infra template?
[05:28] Marcus: roughly, 50% dependency CVEs from container images, 30% infra-as-code template drift (the s3 one), and 20% config/crypto issues (JWT/OpenSSL). We'll provide a mapping in the tracker.
[05:43] Lena: I'm going to share a link in the chat to the remediation tracker — the live sheet where we'll assign owners.
[05:50] [background typing noise; link pasted but not transcribed]
[06:10] Maya: noticed a mention in the report about RBAC — there was a service account with overly broad perms?
[06:16] Marcus: yeah, that was flagged as a high. The service account used for backup ingestion had admin:roles instead of narrower write-only permissions. We recommend principle of least privilege and a short-lived token pattern.
[06:34] Oliver: we use vault for secrets, but some systems still reference static creds in old ENV vars, is that covered?
[06:40] Marcus: it was — we found two containers with ENV secrets in the manifest. Recommended move: sidecar-based secret injection or use the KMS/Secrets manager with mounted creds.
[06:52] Maya: any mention of SSO/SAML misconfig? Our identity team is sensitive about IdP misconfiguration.
[06:57] Priya: only a minor finding: SP-initiated SSO redirect didn't validate RelayState in one test case — medium. We recommend adding RelayState verification and enforcing SAML signature checks.
[07:12] Ethan: for SOC2 evidence we'd need screenshots of the SAML config — can that be exported?
[07:18] Marcus: yes, we'll export the SSO config audit and provide step-by-step docs.
[07:24] Lena: ok, next topic: retest timeline. We propose a two-stage retest — quick validation of the 3 criticals after patch week, then a full retest after the first month of patches. Does that align?
[07:37] Ethan: yes, two-stage is fine. We need to communicate to legal and then schedule.
[07:43] Marcus: note on testing: for shared infra (dedicated) we can run a scoped retest with IP allowlist so it doesn't impact production.
[07:53] Oliver: great. Regarding the JWT fix, is there a recommended library version?
[07:58] Marcus: upgrade to jwtlib 4.2.1+ (we put exact versions in the report), and rotate keys. There's also a patch we suggest to validate alg and enforce accepted-alg headers.
[08:14] Maya: any automation around key rotation? Manual rotation is painful for us.
[08:18] Priya: Redwood supports key rotation APIs; we can perform a rolling rotation that updates signing keys without invalidating existing sessions by phasing in new keys and deprecating the old within 7 days. We'll include sample procedures.
[08:32] Ethan: retention and data residency — our EU customers require that backups of EU tenants stay in eu-west1. The report flagged some backup snapshots in the default region.
[08:42] Marcus: yes, that was a misconfigured backup job that defaulted to us-east-1 region. Fix: set region override in IaC and set retention policies per-tenant. We'll add a migration plan for re-snapshotting EU tenants into eu-west-1.
[08:59] Oliver: what's the risk on the OpenSSL vuln? Is it exploitable remotely?
[09:03] Marcus: in our tests it required a specific cipher negotiation sequence, high complexity but remote — we keep it high severity because of the data sensitivity. Immediate upgrade recommended.
[09:14] Maya: are we tracking all shared libraries in SBOM? We want to show auditors a bill of materials.
[09:20] Marcus: we can generate SBOMs per image and attach them to the tracker; we recommend CI generate SBOM on build and store artifact.
[09:29] Lena: okay, I'm going to read back the major next steps: Redwood will upload full pen-test PDF and raw logs, provide remediation snippets, pipeline examples, and SOC2 evidence bundle. Nova to triage the tracker, assign owners, and schedule patches and the retest. Anything missing?
[09:46] Ethan: please also provide a short note on false positives and the methodology used so our auditors understand vetted items.
[09:52] Marcus: yes, we'll include a methodology appendix and indicators of tested IPs and auth scopes.
[09:58] Maya: one more — we need the expected time to remediate for high severity items for our SLA with customers. Can you provide typical R T T?
[10:05] Priya: typical SLA: critical 24-72 hours, high 7-14 days depending on complexity, medium 30 days. We'll add these suggested remediation windows to the tracker with rationale.
[10:20] Oliver: on the patch rollout — will there be rolling restarts? Any expected downtime?
[10:25] Marcus: rolling restarts only; the JWT key rotation is zero-downtime if done correctly. For the OpenSSL library in base images we suggest building new images and phasing them via the rolling deployment — expect brief instance restarts but no full service outage.
[10:41] Ethan: about evidence for ISO — we need a document that ties together the issue, remediation, verification, and dates. Is that something Redwood provides?
[10:48] Lena: yes, Redwood's compliance team provides a remediation verification template that lists the finding, remediation steps, owner, test method, and verification note. We'll send that.
[10:58] Marcus: also, we recommend you enable more granular RBAC roles in the console — create a backup-ingest role with only S3 write and list permissions, rather than full admin.
[11:10] Maya: will that break existing jobs that expect admin?
[11:12] Oliver: probably, but we can transition via a staging role and audit changes.
[11:20] Marcus: one more item: we found two containers running as root; low complexity fix is to set non-root user in the Dockerfile and enforce in runtime security policies.
[11:30] Maya: noted.
[11:32] Lena: ok, let's capture the explicit deliverables — I'll do that now: file upload (pen-test PDF), remediation tracker, CI snippets, SOC2 evidence bundle, KMS rotation guide, SBOM examples. Anything else?
[11:48] Ethan: a short executive summary tailored for legal that lists customer impact and risk levels — we need that for the board.
[11:55] Lena: we'll add an executive summary.
[12:00] [wrap-up, small talk]
[12:12] Marcus: final note: for the planned retest please open a support ticket with the timeframe and we'll coordinate IP allowlists.
[12:20] Oliver: will do.
[12:25] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing with links and due dates.
[12:30] Ethan: thanks.

End of transcript.
